title: Explain/verify area-to-area movement constraints using entrance/exit layout model (Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, Tipper)
summary: Use the source-backed modular layout rule—each named area has an entrance and an exit—to interpret whether observed AGV/AGB movement between areas (Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, Tipper) follows the expected entrance/exit transition constraint.
when_to_use: When you are troubleshooting or explaining an AGV/AGB’s movement pattern between distinct layout areas and you need to check whether the movement is consistent with the modular entrance/exit constraint for the named areas (Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, Tipper).
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a substitute for system-specific fault isolation when movement cannot be reconciled with the entrance/exit constraint; escalate for deeper investigation.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Apply the entrance/exit layout rule to interpret observed area-to-area movement patterns for the named areas (Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, Tipper).
L1_support: If movement appears to skip the expected area boundary behavior, escalate for deeper system-specific investigation beyond this layout interpretation.
access_or_tools_needed: Visual access to the layout representation used in the live system or the layout example referenced by the source segment
Training video segment evidence for the entrance/exit movement rule and named area types

visual_references.description: Layout design example showing modular/scalable areas with entrance/exit and named area types (Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, Tipper).

steps.title: Identify the relevant layout areas named by the source in the example design: Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, and Tipper
steps.purpose: Establish which distinct areas you will use when interpreting observed AGV/AGB movement patterns.
steps.instruction: From the source’s example layout, note the named area types: Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, and Tipper. Use these as the distinct boundaries for your movement interpretation.
steps.expected_result: You can clearly map the observed movement endpoints to the named areas: Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, and/or Tipper.
steps.healthy_condition: The movement you are analyzing can be described as transitions between these distinct named areas (not ambiguous intermediate spaces).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot confidently classify the observed locations into the named areas, making it unclear which entrance/exit boundary rule should apply.

actions.label: Identify named areas
actions.exact_action: Identify the example layout areas: Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, and Tipper.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Source lists example area types: Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, and Tipper; and describes modular areas connected by entrance and exit.

steps.title: Apply the source rule: to move from one area to another, an AGV/AGB must go to the exit before entering the next area
steps.purpose: Provide the expected entrance/exit transition constraint used to interpret movement between distinct areas.
steps.instruction: Use the modular layout rule stated by the source: when moving from one area to another, the AGV/AGB must go to the exit before entering the next area.
steps.expected_result: Your interpretation framework is set: every area-to-area transition you evaluate should include an exit step before the next area entrance.
steps.healthy_condition: Your planned checks for movement transitions explicitly look for an exit-before-entrance pattern between distinct areas.
steps.failure_condition: You interpret movement as direct area-to-area transitions without considering the required exit-before-entrance constraint.

actions.label: Apply entrance/exit constraint
actions.exact_action: Use the rule: an AGV must go to the exit before entering the next area.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Source explains: layout is modular/scalable with distinct areas connected by a common entrance and exit; to move from one area to another, an AGV must go through an exit to go through an entrance.

steps.title: When observing an item’s movement between areas, check whether the movement pattern is consistent with the entrance/exit constraint described by the source
steps.purpose: Determine whether the observed movement between distinct areas follows the expected modular entrance/exit transition behavior.
steps.instruction: For the observed AGV/AGB movement between the named areas (Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, Tipper), verify that the transition includes the exit-before-entrance behavior implied by the modular layout rule.
steps.expected_result: You can conclude whether the observed movement pattern is consistent with the entrance/exit constraint (exit occurs before the next area entrance).
steps.healthy_condition: Observed transitions between distinct areas can be described as: exit from the prior area, then entrance into the next area.
steps.failure_condition: Observed movement appears to skip the expected exit-before-entrance behavior between distinct areas.

actions.label: Check transition order
actions.exact_action: Check that movement from one area to another goes to the exit before entering the next area.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Source states the entrance/exit constraint for moving between distinct areas.

steps.title: If movement appears to skip an area boundary, re-check that the observation is between distinct areas that have entrance/exit points in the described modular layout
steps.purpose: Avoid false positives by confirming that the observation truly represents transitions between the distinct modular areas described by the source.
steps.instruction: If the observed movement seems to skip the expected boundary behavior, re-check that the movement you are interpreting is actually between distinct areas (Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, Tipper) that follow the modular entrance/exit model.
steps.expected_result: Either (a) you reconcile the observation with the exit-before-entrance constraint by correctly identifying the distinct areas, or (b) you confirm the movement cannot be reconciled with the constraint.
steps.healthy_condition: After re-checking area classification, the movement can be described as consistent with exit-before-entrance between the correct distinct areas.
steps.failure_condition: Even after re-checking area classification, the movement still cannot be reconciled with the entrance/exit constraint between distinct areas.

actions.label: Re-validate area boundaries
actions.exact_action: Re-check that the observation is between distinct areas that have entrance/exit points in the modular layout model.

stop_or_escalate_if: If observed movement cannot be reconciled with the entrance/exit constraint described by the source, escalate for deeper system-specific investigation beyond this layout explanation.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Source defines the modular layout rule and the named distinct areas used for entrance/exit transitions.

success_criteria: You correctly identify the relevant distinct areas (Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, Tipper) for the movement you are analyzing.
You apply the entrance/exit transition rule to interpret whether observed movement is consistent with exit-before-entrance between distinct areas.
If movement cannot be reconciled with the rule, you escalate for deeper system-specific investigation.
healthy_conditions: Observed transitions between distinct areas can be described as exit from the prior area followed by entrance into the next area.
Area classification matches the named modular areas used by the source (Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, Tipper).
failure_conditions: Observed movement appears to skip the exit-before-entrance behavior between distinct areas.
Area classification is ambiguous such that you cannot determine which entrance/exit constraint should apply.
escalation_guidance: If observed movement cannot be reconciled with the entrance/exit constraint described by the source, escalate for deeper system-specific investigation beyond this layout explanation.
